analysis.executiveSummary: Ravens Regime proposes sending WR Jaylen Waddle and WR Deebo Samuel Sr. to Mile High Royal Lions for TE Travis Kelce, a 2027 2nd (King Jesus), and a 2028 1st (Mile High). While acquiring Kelce fills a massive TE void for Ravens Regime (+57.4 C-AVI starting boost at TE) and nets premium draft capital, the submitted package creates an unacceptable lineup downgrade (-15.3 net C-AVI) and capital drain for Mile High Royal Lions, who are also actively in an 'Increase Playoff Odds' window. To make this deal negotiable, Ravens Regime must send additional premium draft capital (such as a 2029 1st) to balance the asset equation.

analysis.executiveSummary: Ravens Regime seeks to improve near-term playoff odds by acquiring 23-year-old Carolina wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (C-AVI 86.1, D-AVI 95.0) from Southside Savages. The submitted foundation package of Deebo Samuel Sr. (C-AVI 38.4), Jaylen Waddle (C-AVI 54.0), and Kyle Monangai (C-AVI 49.5) creates an immediate starting lineup increase of +32.1 C-AVI points for Ravens Regime, placing McMillan into WR1 over Waddle. However, Southside Savages is operating under a Retool strategy; surrendering a healthy 23-year-old WR1 for two older receivers (Deebo, age 30; Waddle, age 27) and a depth RB without receiving draft pick capital conflicts with their organizational goal. To achieve a deal that Southside Savages will accept, Ravens Regime must revise the proposal by attaching premium draft capital—specifically their 2029 1st-round pick (Pick AVI 79.3)—while retaining all requested foundation assets.
